correctness.rationale: From the actual package definitions, conditioning on which walk and index is updated gives E[epsilon(t+1)|epsilon(t)]=(I-L_m/(2m))epsilon(t) for one walk, where L_m is mixed Neumann/antisymmetric terminal Laplacian, diag 1,2,...,2,3 (m=1: [2]), off diag -1. IID centered starting increments give C=1^T P^t 1/m. Verified half-integer cosine ghost boundary eigenvectors and their squared projections 1/[2m^2 sin^2(theta/2)], all nonnegative bases and sum-one coefficients. Exact Green vector x_j=(m^2-j(j-1))/2 solves Lx=1, sum yields cubic formula. Fixed-k eigenvalue limit under t/m^3->s plus O((k-1/2)^-2) summable weights prove F(s), including s=0. F is continuous strictly decreasing (F(0)=1, F(infinity)=0), so every fixed threshold has unique cubic crossing. M=1 and extra-inert convention are correctly handled. Independently constructed full finite-state rational Markov kernels at m=1..7 for both update clocks, compared 12 lags per case to exact conditional expectations and numerical spectral formula, 350 checks; independent exact Git tree reconstruction and high-precision F threshold bisections support finite constants, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: This exact, size-uniform endpoint time-correlation law answers a specifically posed recent numerical exponent question for a natural two-walk representation of meandric systems. The nontrivial full scaling curve, lag-integral Green polynomial, explicit threshold constants and sampling-clock distinction are mathematically useful benchmarks for isolating endpoint transport from as-yet-unanswered crossing-event fluctuations. Even though Fourier diagonalization/exclusion duality are classical methods, the precise conjecture resolution and quantitative normalizations are not a mere renaming or textbook tautology.

final_claim: For every integer m>=1, stationary independent fair +/-1 walk increments with top/bottom and uniform-index local swap/free-terminal flip dynamics have normalized top-endpoint covariance C_m(t)=sum_{k=1}^m [2m^2 sin^2((k-1/2)pi/(2m))]^{-1}[1-(1-cos((k-1/2)pi/m))/m]^t, all integer t>=0 (including m=1, t=0). Its lag sum is m(2m^2+1)/3. For all t_m/m^3->s in [0,infinity) the limit is F(s)=sum_{k>=1}2 exp(-pi^2(k-1/2)^2 s/2)/(pi^2(k-1/2)^2), with nontrivial threshold scales m^3. If an additional inert index 0 is sampled, replace m by m+1 only in the decay eigenvalue denominators, sum=(m+1)(2m^2+1)/3 and same F.
limitations: Finite-state numerical checks are bounded to m<=7 and lags<12; they are not infinite-volume proofs.
Novelty is best-of-knowledge with real risk of an unindexed older exact finite SSEP correlation formula; no independence or outside certification claimed.
Only stationary one-walk endpoint autocorrelation under terminal flip and specified two-walk update clock; neither crossing-event decorrelation nor overall full-meandric-map mixing is proved.
Asymptotic profile is for finite scaled time s>=0 and fixed nontrivial thresholds, not uniform over unbounded s.
The inert-index clock changes finite m constants but retains the same limiting profile.
